headword: {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}

definitions.explanation: A person who has just joined a company. In Japan, most new employees start in April after graduating from university. Composed of 新入 (newly entering) + 社員 (company employee). Often abbreviated to 新人 in casual speech.

examples.japanese: {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}って→入る：00494_hairu⟧きた。
{新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}{研修|けんしゅう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}⟦かかる→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧。
examples.english: New employee training takes one month.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今年|ことし}→今年：00722_kotoshi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{即戦力|そくせんりょく}→即戦力：17917_sokusenryoku⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{期待|きたい}→期待：00238_kitai⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: This year's new employees are expected to contribute immediately.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese corporate culture, {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん} specifically refers to employees in their first year at a company, typically fresh graduates who start in April. They are expected to learn workplace etiquette and culture through formal training (⟦{研修|けんしゅう}→研修：05322_kenshuu⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}{研修|けんしゅう} (new employee training)
- {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}⟦{歓迎会|かんげいかい}→歓迎会：15791_kangeikai⟧ (welcome party for new employees)
- {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{迎|むか}える→迎える：01193_mukaeru⟧ (to welcome new employees)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Every April, companies hold ⟦{入社式|にゅうしゃしき}→入社式：18833_nyuushashiki⟧ (joining ceremonies) for new hires. Media surveys of {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん} attitudes are a spring tradition in Japan.
